writingModel: This is going to be one of the most important years of my life at WKU. I am now in my second year, and the decisions I make this year are going to have a real impact on my future career and personal development. Last year, I learned a lot — but I also made mistakes. I spent too much time on things that did not matter, and not enough time on the things that did. This year is going to be different. I have made a clear, honest plan — and I am going to follow it.

Academically, I am going to work much harder than last year. I am going to attend every lecture without exception — no more skipping Tuesday morning classes because I am tired! I am going to spend at least ninety minutes every evening reviewing my notes from the day. In September, I am going to start preparing for the WKU Academic Excellence Scholarship — the application deadline is the fifteenth of October, and I am going to submit a strong application well before the deadline. I am also going to join the student research group in my faculty. It is going to take time and effort, but it is going to be worth it.

Professionally, I am going to do everything I can to gain real experience before I graduate. I am going to apply for at least two internship programmes this year — one during the winter break and one during the summer. I know that competition for internships is very strong, so I am going to prepare a professional CV and a well-written cover letter in advance. I am also going to improve my English every day — not just in lectures, but by reading English articles about my field, watching documentaries without subtitles, and speaking with my international classmates as often as possible.

On a personal level, I am going to learn to code in Python this year. I have been curious about programming for a long time, and this is finally the year I am going to start. I found an excellent free course online — I am going to spend thirty minutes every morning on it, before breakfast. I am also going to manage my money much more carefully. I am going to put five thousand tenge aside every month and not touch it until the end of the year. By December, I will have sixty thousand tenge saved — enough for a good new laptop or a short trip that I can plan as a reward for a hard year of work.

My biggest goal for this year is both simple and demanding: I am going to become someone who is genuinely proud of their own efforts. I am not going to make excuses. I am not going to say "I will start next week" when I can start today. I will work hard, stay focused on what matters, and take care of my health and my closest relationships. I know that at this time next year, I will look back at this moment — sitting here writing these plans — and I will feel satisfied with what I have achieved. That is my promise to myself. And I am going to keep it.
